sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 4.5% a year from $70.3 billion in FY2016 to $104.8 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F205].
The shape is a step change, not a compounding: revenue jumped 19.8% in FY2020 and 13.3% in FY2021, then fell 1.6%, 0.8% and 1.7% in FY2023 through FY2025 [D183][D230][D324][D370][D416].
The FY2020 jump came from a 19.3% comparable sales increase, with digitally originated comparable sales up 146% in the second through fourth quarters [P51][P53].
The FY2022 collapse, with operating margin down 4.9pp to 3.5%, reflected discretionary category sales decreases and the cost of clearing elevated inventory [D290][F31][P38].
Merchandise sales were 98.0% of revenue in FY2025 and contributed -2.0pp to the year's decline [D465][D467].
Food & beverage was the only large category to grow in FY2025, up 1.3% and adding 0.3pp, while apparel fell 4.7% and subtracted 0.7pp [D507][D508][D564][D565].
Comparable sales fell 2.6% in FY2025 on a 2.2% traffic decrease and a 0.4% lower average transaction [P14].
Operating costs grew 0.4pp faster than revenue in FY2025 [D439].
Net income fell 9.4% while diluted EPS fell 8.2%, as the diluted share count dropped 1.3% [D418][D420][D434].
Operating margin was 4.9% in FY2025, below the 5.6% window median and far below the 8.4% FY2021 high [F34][D590][D589].
The FY2025 margin fell 0.3pp, with cost of revenue taking 0.3pp and SG&A adding 0.1pp [D429][D440][D441].
The gross margin rate slipped to 27.9% from 28.2%, and the SG&A rate held at 20.6% including a 0.6pp interchange settlement benefit [P12][P11].
In FY2025 net margin of 3.5% sat 1.3pp below the 4.9% operating margin, with a 22.3% effective tax rate [F54][F34][D629][D403].
Operating cash flow of $6.56 billion was 1.77x net income in FY2025, below the 2.01x window median [F84][F44][D404][D619].
The decline from $7.37 billion in FY2024 reflected lower net earnings and lower accounts payable leverage [F83][P7].
Free cash flow fell to $2.84 billion, a 2.7% margin against a 4.5% window median, as capex rose 28.9% to $3.73 billion [F104][D401][D596][F94][D423].
The capex increase primarily reflected more investment in new stores and remodels [P5].
Cash was $5.49 billion against long-term debt of $14.4 billion in FY2025, and the current ratio was 0.94x [F144][F194][F184].
The current ratio matched its 0.94x window median but sat below the 1.03x FY2020 high [F184][D602][D601].

Buybacks plus dividends of $2.46 billion were 86.8% of free cash flow, and return on average equity of 24.0% ranked at the 40th percentile of five retail peers against a 28.6% median [D412][D413][D415][D616][D617].
Share repurchases slowed to $408 million from $7.36 billion in FY2021, and the diluted count fell 1.3% [X126][X122][D434].
Revenue has declined three years running, from $109.1 billion in FY2022 to $104.8 billion in FY2025 [R1][F7][F10].
A three-year top-line slide with operating margin below its window median leaves little room for cost deleverage [R1][F34][D590].
The current ratio was 0.94x in FY2025, below 1.0x [R2][F184].
A sub-1.0x current ratio is normal for this model but leaves working capital dependent on payables terms [R2][F184].
The pack's cash and debt lines carry disclosed breaks: short-term investments sit inside cash, and current debt sits inside long-term debt in FY2016-FY2018 [R7][R8].
Net cash and total-debt comparisons across those years are not usable, so the balance-sheet read rests on the reported lines [R7][R8].
Whether operating margin in the FY2026 10-K holds above the 4.9% FY2025 level or falls toward the 3.5% FY2022 low [F34][D588].
Whether free cash flow margin recovers toward the 4.5% window median from 2.7% in FY2025, given guidance of about $5 billion of FY2026 capex [D401][D596][P4].
Whether revenue growth in the FY2026 10-K turns positive from the -1.7% of FY2025 [D416].
